description.narrative: Since the beginning of 2025, the Ministry of Health, in collaboration with the World Health Organisation (WHO) and United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF), has reported a significant increase in cholera cases throughout the country. As of 18 July 2025, more than 35,000 suspected cases of cholera had been recorded in 17 of the island's 36 provinces. According to the WHO, between 1 January and 8 June 2025, 29,392 suspected cases of cholera and 620 deaths were reported, with a mortality rate of 2%. Kinshasa remains one of the most affected areas, with the WHO deploying cholera supplies and providing emergency beds to health facilities in Kinshasa. This crisis is exacerbated by systemic vulnerabilities, including overcrowding, inadequate sanitation infrastructure and widespread dependence on unsafe water sources. Overcrowding in densely populated urban areas creates an ideal environment for the proliferation of cholera -causing bacteria, leading to open defecation and environmental contamination. A critical lack of public awareness about cholera transmission, prevention, and timely medical intervention further complicates these issues. Oxfam's response aims to raise awareness, ensure access to safe water and sanitation, and strengthen local health institutions to prepare for future outbreaks among 50,000 people in various communities, including vulnerable populations at risk due to poor sanitation and limited access to healthcare. The initiative builds on Oxfam's previous public health programmes, such as Ebola, MPox, and Cholera. The organisation has successfully implemented public health initiatives during previous epidemics such as Covid and Cholera, building trust within local communities, which is crucial for effective engagement during the current cholera crisis. The aim is to reduce cholera -related morbidity and mortality among vulnerable populations in Kinshasa by improving immediate access to safe drinking water, sanitation, hygiene and community prevention ove
